results.title: Formally orthogonal polynomial family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a field. A family $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of polynomials over $R$ is formally orthogonal if there is an $R$-linear functional $L \colon R[x] \to R$ such that each $p_n$ has degree $n$, $L(p_n p_m) = 0$ whenever $n \ne m$, and $L(p_n^2) \ne 0$ for every $n$.

results.title: Favard's theorem, forward direction
results.caption: Theorem

Then there are sequences $(\alpha_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(\beta_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $R$ with $\beta_n \ne 0$ for all $n \ge 1$ such that $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, and $p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) \, p_n - \beta_n \, p_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.

results.title: Favard's theorem

results.title: Euler–Fermat congruence modulo prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $a$, every prime $p$ and every natural number $r \ge 1$, we have $a^{p^r} \equiv a^{p^{r-1}} \pmod{p^r}$.

results.title: Euler–Fermat congruence modulo prime powers, for positive bases

results.title: Orders lie in the ring of integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $O$ an order in $K$, that is, a subring of $K$ contained in the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ (the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$) whose field of fractions is $K$. Then $O \subseteq \mathcal{O}_K$.

results.title: The fraction field of an order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $O$ an order in $K$, that is, a subring of $K$ contained in the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ (the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$) whose field of fractions is $K$. Then $K$, with the inclusion $O \subseteq K$, is a field of fractions of $O$.

results.title: Elements of a number field are quotients of elements of an order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $O$ an order in $K$, that is, a subring of $K$ contained in the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ (the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$) whose field of fractions is $K$. Then for every $x \in K$ there are $a, b \in O$ with $b \neq 0$ and $x = a / b$.

results.title: The ring of integers is an order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every number field $K$, the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$, is an order in $K$, that is, a subring of $K$ contained in $\mathcal{O}_K$ whose field of fractions is $K$.

results.title: Carmichael numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is a Carmichael number if $n > 1$, $n$ is not prime, and $a^n \equiv a \pmod{n}$ for every natural number $a$.

results.title: Carmichael numbers via the residue ring

results.title: Korselt's criterion
results.caption: Theorem

Then there are infinitely many Carmichael numbers $n$ whose number of prime factors counted with multiplicity, $\Omega(n)$, is prime.

results.title: Spectrum of an accretive operator has nonnegative real part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $\operatorname{Re}\langle Tu, u\rangle \ge 0$ for every $u \in H$, then every element $\mu$ of the spectrum of $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re}\mu \ge 0$.

results.title: Positivity iff spectrum nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a self-adjoint bounded linear operator on a nonzero Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Then $\operatorname{Re}\langle Tu, u\rangle \ge 0$ for every $u \in H$ if and only if every element $\mu$ of the spectrum of $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re}\mu \ge 0$.

results.title: Rayleigh quotient of a shifted operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on an inner product space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $I$ be the identity operator on $H$, and write $R_S(x) = \operatorname{Re}\langle Sx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$ for the Rayleigh quotient of an operator $S$. Then for every real number $t$ and every nonzero $x \in H$, $R_{tI - T}(x) = t - R_T(x)$.

results.title: Spectrum bounds over nonzero vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a self-adjoint bounded linear operator on a nonzero Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with Rayleigh quotient $R_T(x) = \operatorname{Re}\langle Tx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$. Then every $\mu$ in the spectrum of $T$ satisfies $\inf_{x \ne 0} R_T(x) \le \operatorname{Re}\mu \le \sup_{x \ne 0} R_T(x)$, where the infimum and supremum range over the nonzero vectors $x \in H$.

results.title: Spectrum bounds over all vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a self-adjoint bounded linear operator on a nonzero Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with Rayleigh quotient $R_T(x) = \operatorname{Re}\langle Tx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$ for $x \ne 0$ and $R_T(0) = 0$. Then every $\mu$ in the spectrum of $T$ satisfies $\inf_{x \in H} R_T(x) \le \operatorname{Re}\mu \le \sup_{x \in H} R_T(x)$.

results.title: Convolution on a finite abelian group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. The convolution of functions $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is the function $f * g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$, with no normalizing factor $1/|G|$, where $|G|$ is the number of elements of $G$.

results.title: Convolution on a finite abelian group is commutative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite abelian group $G$ and functions $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$, we have $f * g = g * f$, where the convolution is $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$.

results.title: Convolution on a finite abelian group is associative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite abelian group $G$ and functions $f, g, h : G \to \mathbb{C}$, we have $(f * g) * h = f * (g * h)$, where the convolution is $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$.

results.title: The delta function is a left identity for convolution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $\delta_0 : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be the function with $\delta_0(0) = 1$ and $\delta_0(y) = 0$ for $y \ne 0$. Then $\delta_0 * g = g$ for every $g : G \to \mathbb{C}$, where the convolution is $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$.

results.title: Young's convolution inequality on a finite abelian group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and, for $u : G \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $s > 0$, write $\|u\|_s = \left(\sum_{x \in G} |u(x)|^s\right)^{1/s}$. Let $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $p, q, r$ be real numbers with $p > 1$, $q > 1$, $r > 1$ and $1/p + 1/q = 1 + 1/r$. Then the convolution $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$ satisfies $\|f * g\|_r \le \|f\|_p \, \|g\|_q$.

results.title: Tauber's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Tauber's theorem (1897). If the power series `∑ aₙ rⁿ` converges (in the Abel sense) to `A` as `r → 1⁻` and `n * aₙ → 0`, then the partial sums of `a` converge to `A`.

results.title: Hardy–Littlewood Tauberian theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Hardy–Littlewood Tauberian theorem (1914). If `aₙ ≥ 0` and the power series `∑ aₙ rⁿ` converges for every `r ∈ (0, 1)` with Abel limit `A` as `r → 1⁻`, then the partial sums of `a` converge to `A`.

results.title: Lacunary sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $(m_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers is lacunary when $m_n > 0$ for every $n$ and there is a real number $\lambda > 1$ such that $m_{n+1} \ge \lambda m_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.

results.title: Sets of topological recurrence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of topological recurrence when it is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for $\ell = 1$.

results.title: Topological recurrence is $1$-topological recurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of topological recurrence if and only if it is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for $\ell = 1$.

results.title: Sets of multiple topological recurrence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of multiple topological recurrence when it is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for every natural number $\ell \ge 1$.

results.title: Characterization of multiple topological recurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of multiple topological recurrence if and only if $D$ is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for every natural number $\ell \ge 1$.

results.title: Chromatically intersective sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is chromatically intersective if every element of $D$ is positive and, for every natural number $r \ge 1$ and every coloring of the positive integers with $r$ colors, there are positive integers $a$ and $b$ of the same color whose difference $a - b$, computed in the integers, lies in $D$.

results.title: Characterization of chromatically intersective sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is chromatically intersective if and only if every element of $D$ is positive and, for every natural number $r \ge 1$ and every coloring of the positive integers with $r$ colors, there are positive integers $a$ and $b$ of the same color whose difference $a - b$, computed in the integers, lies in $D$.

results.title: Positive Fibonacci set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The positive Fibonacci set is $\{F_n : n \ge 2\}$, where the Fibonacci numbers are $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$ and $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$. Equivalently, it is the set $\{1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots\}$ of positive Fibonacci numbers, each counted once.

results.title: Membership in the positive Fibonacci set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $F_n$ for the $n$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. A natural number $d$ belongs to the positive Fibonacci set if and only if $d = F_n$ for some natural number $n \ge 2$.

results.title: Even Fibonacci set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F_m$ denote the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. The even Fibonacci set is $\{F_{3n+3} : n \ge 0\}$; its first terms are $2, 8, 34, \dots$.

results.title: Membership in the even Fibonacci set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $F_m$ for the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. A natural number $d$ belongs to the even Fibonacci set if and only if $d = F_{3n+3}$ for some natural number $n$.

results.title: Growth bound for the degree of accessibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \ge 2$, let $d_0 < d_1 < d_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers with $d_0 > 0$, and let $D = \{d_n : n \ge 0\}$. If there are a real number $\delta > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 1$ such that $d_{n+1} \ge \left(2 + \frac{1}{r-1} + \delta\right) d_n$ for every $n \ge N - 1$, then $D$ is not $r$-accessible.

results.title: Fast eventual growth rules out 2-accessibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d_0 < d_1 < d_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers with $d_0 > 0$, and let $D = \{d_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$. Suppose there are a real number $\delta > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that $d_{n+1} \ge (3 + \delta) d_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n + 1 \ge N$. Then $D$ is not $2$-accessible.

results.title: 2-large sets contain multiples of every positive integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every $2$-large set $D$ of positive integers contains a multiple of each positive integer $m$.

results.title: Finite removal preserves $r$-largeness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number. If a set $D \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is $r$-large and $F \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is finite, then $D \setminus F$ is $r$-large.

results.title: Largeness is partition regular
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $D_1, D_2 \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and their union $D = D_1 \cup D_2$ is large, then $D_1$ is large or $D_2$ is large.

results.title: Sets growing by a factor of three are not 2-large
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d_0 < d_1 < d_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers with $d_0 > 0$ and $d_{n+1} \ge 3 d_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $D = \{d_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$. Then $D$ is not $2$-large.

results.title: Dilates of a finite union of lacunary sets stay away from the integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\ell \ge 1$ and let $S_0, \dots, S_{\ell-1} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be lacunary sets with union $S = \bigcup_i S_i$. Then there are real numbers $\alpha$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the infimum over $s \in S$ of the distance $|\alpha s - \operatorname{round}(\alpha s)|$ from $\alpha s$ to its nearest integer $\operatorname{round}(\alpha s)$ equals $\varepsilon$.

results.title: Two-colorings avoiding long $D$-progressions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be a set of positive integers, let $\alpha$ be a real number and let $\varepsilon > 0$ be such that $\lVert \alpha d \rVert \ge \varepsilon$ for every $d \in D$, where $\lVert t \rVert$ denotes the distance from $t$ to the nearest integer. Then there is a $2$-coloring of the positive integers with no monochromatic $D$-arithmetic progression of length $\lceil 1/(2\varepsilon) \rceil + 1$.

results.title: Finite unions of lacunary sets are not 2-large
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all lacunary sets $D_1, \dots, D_n$, the union $D_1 \cup \dots \cup D_n$ is not 2-large.

results.title: Positive values of a polynomial vanishing at zero form a large set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients, positive leading coefficient and $p(0) = 0$. Then the set of positive integers $d$ such that $p(n) = d$ for some positive integer $n$ is large.

results.title: A coloring criterion for accessibility of a shifted set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \ge 2$ and $c$ be natural numbers, let $D$ be a set of positive integers, and write $D + c = \{d + c : d \in D\}$. Suppose that for every coloring of $D$ with $r - 1$ colors and every $k \ge 1$ there are $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1} \in D$, all of the same color, that form a $(D + c)$-diffsequence, that is, $x_{i+1} - x_i \in D + c$ for every $i < k - 1$. Then $D + c$ is $r$-accessible.

results.title: Sets containing their own long diffsequences are 2-accessible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be a set of positive integers. If for every $k \ge 1$ there are positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$, all in $D$, that form a $D$-diffsequence, then $D$ is $2$-accessible.

results.title: Integral quotients of an accessible set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$ and $r$ be natural numbers and let $A$ be a set of natural numbers. If $A$ is $rd$-accessible, then the set $\{n \ge 1 : nd \in A\}$, that is, the positive integers of the form $a/d$ with $a \in A$, is $r$-accessible.

results.title: Multiples of $d$ in an accessible set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$ and $r$ be natural numbers and let $A$ be a set of natural numbers. If $A$ is $rd$-accessible, then the set $\{a \in A : d \mid a\}$ of members of $A$ divisible by $d$ is $r$-accessible.

results.summary: Let $D$, $D_1$ and $D_2$ be sets of natural numbers with $D = D_1 \cup D_2$. If $D$ is accessible, then $D_1$ is accessible or $D_2$ is accessible.

results.title: Monochromatic finite sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a colouring $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, r - 1\}$ of the natural numbers with $r$ colours, a finite sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers is monochromatic when all its terms have the same colour: $c(x_i) = c(x_j)$ for all $i, j < k$.

results.title: Finite $S$-diffsequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $S$ of natural numbers, a finite sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers is an $S$-diffsequence when each term is the previous one plus an element of $S$: for every $i$ with $i + 1 < k$ there is $d \in S$ with $x_{i+1} = x_i + d$.

results.title: $r$-accessible sets of natural numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is $r$-accessible when for every colouring $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, r - 1\}$ with $r$ colours and every length $k \ne 1$ there is a sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers that is monochromatic for $c$ and is an $S$-diffsequence: for each $i$ with $i + 1 < k$ there is $d \in S$ with $x_{i+1} = x_i + d$.

results.title: 2-accessibility of the primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that the set of prime numbers is $2$-accessible: for every colouring $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$ of the natural numbers with two colours and every length $k \ne 1$ there is a sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers, all of the same colour, such that each difference $x_{i+1} - x_i$ is a prime number. Open Problem Garden question OPG-1797 asks whether this holds.

results.title: The primes are 2-accessible

results.title: Classical Ramsey numbers

results.title: Interpretation of a grammar symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Under an assignment $V$ of languages to nonterminals, a terminal $a$ denotes the language containing only the one-letter word $a$, and a nonterminal $A$ denotes its assigned language $V(A)$.

results.title: Interpretation of a sentential form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Under an assignment $V$ of languages to nonterminals, a sentential form denotes the concatenation, in order, of the languages its symbols denote: a terminal $a$ denotes the language containing only the one-letter word $a$, and a nonterminal $A$ denotes $V(A)$. The empty sentential form denotes the language containing only the empty word.

results.title: Interpretation of a concatenation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every assignment $V$ of languages to nonterminals and all sentential forms $u$ and $v$, the language that $uv$ denotes under $V$ is the concatenation of the languages that $u$ and $v$ denote under $V$.

results.title: A terminal word denotes its singleton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under every assignment of languages to nonterminals, a terminal word $w$, read as a sentential form, denotes the singleton language $\{w\}$.

results.title: Valuation of a grammar
results.caption: Definition

Interpret a sentential form under $V$ by sending each terminal $a$ to the language $\{a\}$ of the one-letter word $a$ and each nonterminal $B$ to $V(B)$, and concatenating these languages in order (the empty form is interpreted as $\{\varepsilon\}$). Then $V$ is a *valuation* of $g$ when, for…

results.title: A production step shrinks interpretations under a valuation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $V$ a valuation of $g$. If a sentential form $u$ rewrites to $v$ by one production of $g$, then the language that $v$ denotes under $V$ is contained in the language that $u$ denotes under $V$.

results.title: Derivations shrink interpretations under a valuation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $V$ a valuation of $g$. If a sentential form $u$ derives $v$ in $g$ (in zero or more steps), then the language that $v$ denotes under $V$ is contained in the language that $u$ denotes under $V$.

results.title: Valuations bound the language of a grammar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$ and every valuation $V$ of $g$, the language generated by $g$ is contained in $V(S)$, where $S$ is the initial nonterminal of $g$.

results.title: Concatenating derivations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and let $u$, $u'$, $v$, $v'$ be sentential forms of $g$. If $u$ derives $u'$ and $v$ derives $v'$ in $g$ (each in zero or more steps), then the concatenation $uv$ derives $u'v'$ in $g$.

results.title: Renaming the nonterminals of a symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a map $f$ from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, renaming a grammar symbol by $f$ leaves a terminal $a$ unchanged and sends a nonterminal $A$ to the nonterminal $f(A)$.

results.title: Renaming the nonterminals of a production
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a map $f$ from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, the renaming by $f$ of a production $A \to u$ is the production $f(A) \to u'$, where $u'$ is obtained from $u$ by replacing each nonterminal $B$ with $f(B)$ and leaving each terminal unchanged.

results.title: Interpretation after renaming nonterminals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon N \to N'$ be a map of nonterminals, extended to sentential forms by renaming each nonterminal and keeping each terminal, and let $V$ assign a language to each nonterminal in $N'$. For every sentential form $u$ over $N$, the language that $f(u)$ denotes under $V$ equals the language that $u$ denotes under the assignment $V \circ f$.

results.title: Language generated from a nonterminal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ and a nonterminal $A$ of $g$, the language generated by $g$ from $A$ is the set of words $w$ over the terminals of $g$ such that $g$ derives $w$ from the one-symbol sentential form $A$. It is the language of $g$ with $A$ in place of the initial nonterminal.

results.title: Words of the canonical interpretation are derivable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and assign to each nonterminal $A$ of $g$ the language of terminal words that $g$ derives from $A$. If a terminal word $w$ lies in the language that a sentential form $u$ of $g$ denotes under this assignment, then $u$ derives $w$ in $g$.

results.title: The languages generated from each nonterminal form a valuation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, the assignment that sends each nonterminal $A$ of $g$ to the language generated by $g$ from $A$ is a valuation of $g$.

results.title: Injective renamings are injective on symbols
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $f$ is an injective map from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, then renaming grammar symbols by $f$, which fixes each terminal and sends each nonterminal $A$ to $f(A)$, is injective.

results.title: Injective renamings are injective on productions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $f$ is an injective map from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, then renaming the nonterminals of productions over $N$ by $f$ is injective: two productions with the same renaming are equal.

results.title: Renaming nonterminals fixes terminal words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ map nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, and let $w$ be a word over the terminals. Reading $w$ as a sentential form over $N$ and renaming its nonterminals by $f$ gives $w$ read as a sentential form over $N'$.

results.title: The empty language is context-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty language over any alphabet is context-free: take a grammar with no productions.

results.title: The language of the empty word is context-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $T$, the language over $T$ whose only word is the empty word is context-free: a grammar with one nonterminal and a single production erasing it generates this language.

results.title: Singleton languages are context-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every word $w$ over an alphabet $T$, the language $\{w\}$ consisting of $w$ alone is context-free: one production spells the word out.

results.title: Yield of a sentential form
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ with terminal alphabet $T$, the relation "the sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w$" is the smallest relation such that: the empty form yields the empty word; if $u$ yields $w$, then for every terminal $a$ the form $a u$ yields $a w$; and if $A \to \alpha$ is a production of $g$, $\alpha$ yields $w_1$ and $u$ yields $w_2$, then the form $A u$ yields $w_1 w_2$.

results.title: Concatenation of yields
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w_1$ and the sentential form $v$ yields the terminal word $w_2$, then the concatenated form $u v$ yields $w_1 w_2$.

results.title: Splitting a yield over a concatenation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the concatenated sentential form $u v$ yields the terminal word $w$, then there are terminal words $w_1$ and $w_2$ with $w = w_1 w_2$ such that $u$ yields $w_1$ and $v$ yields $w_2$.

results.title: Yield through one production
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $A \to \alpha$ a production of $g$. If $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$, then the one-symbol sentential form $A$ yields $w$.

results.title: Yields are derivable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w$, then $u$ derives $w$, read as a string of terminal symbols, in $g$: that is, $u \Rightarrow^* w$ in zero or more rewriting steps.

results.title: Derivable terminal words are yields
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the sentential form $u$ derives the terminal word $w$, read as a string of terminal symbols, in $g$, then $u$ yields $w$.

results.title: Yields coincide with derivations of terminal words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, $u$ a sentential form of $g$ and $w$ a word of terminals. Then $u$ yields $w$ in $g$ if and only if $u$ derives in $g$, by zero or more rewriting steps, the sentential form consisting of the letters of $w$ read as terminals.

results.title: Language membership through yields
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar with initial nonterminal $S$. A terminal word $w$ belongs to the language of $g$ if and only if the one-symbol sentential form $S$ yields $w$.

results.title: Classical solution of the linearized reaction-diffusion system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `w` is a classical solution of the linearized reaction-diffusion system `w_t = D w_xx + J w` on `ℝ × ℝ`: `w(t, ·)` is twice differentiable with first and second derivatives `wx`, `wxx`, and `w(·, x)` is differentiable with the prescribed time derivative.

results.title: Dispersion polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dispersion polynomial `h(q) = d_u d_v q² - (d_v f_u + d_u g_v) q + det J`, so that `det (J - k² D) = h(k²)` (`det_modeMatrix`).

results.title: Squared critical wavenumber
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The squared critical wavenumber `k_c² = (d_v f_u + d_u g_v) / (2 d_u d_v)`, the minimizer of the dispersion polynomial (meaningful for `d_u, d_v > 0`; division by zero gives `0`).

results.title: Discriminant of the dispersion polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The discriminant `(d_v f_u + d_u g_v)² - 4 d_u d_v det J` of the dispersion polynomial.

results.title: Lower end of the unstable wavenumber band
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Lower end `q₋ = (S - √Δ) / (2 d_u d_v)` of the unstable band of squared wavenumbers, where `S = d_v f_u + d_u g_v` and `Δ = bandDiscriminant` (meaningful when `0 < Δ`, `d_u, d_v > 0`).

results.title: Upper end of the unstable wavenumber band
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Upper end `q₊ = (S + √Δ) / (2 d_u d_v)` of the unstable band of squared wavenumbers (meaningful when `0 < Δ`, `d_u, d_v > 0`).

results.title: Neumann wavenumber on an interval
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Neumann wavenumber `k_n = n π / L` of the mode `cos(n π x / L)` on `[0, L]`. Meaningful only for `0 < L`; at `L = 0` the totalized division gives `0`, so every labeled Neumann mode collapses to the homogeneous mode.

results.title: Trace of the mode matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `tr (J - k² D) = tr J - k² (d_u + d_v)`.

results.title: Determinant of the mode matrix is the dispersion polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `det (J - k² D) = h(k²)`.

results.title: Routh–Hurwitz for `2 × 2` matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A real `2 × 2` matrix has a complex eigenvalue with positive real part iff its trace is positive or its determinant is negative.

results.title: Instability criterion for a Fourier mode via trace and determinant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Mode `k` is unstable iff `0 < tr (J - k² D)` or `det (J - k² D) < 0`.

results.title: Dispersion relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Fourier mode `e^{μ t} cos(k x) v` is a classical solution of the linearized system `w_t = D w_xx + J w` iff `(J - k² D) v = μ v`.

results.title: Amplitude of a Fourier mode
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The amplitude of a Fourier mode: `‖w(t, 0)‖ = e^{Re μ · t} ‖v‖`.

results.title: Fourier mode is largest at the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `‖w(t, 0)‖` is the amplitude of the mode: `‖w(t, x)‖ ≤ ‖w(t, 0)‖` for every `x`.

results.title: Fourier mode grows unboundedly iff its growth rate is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A nonzero Fourier mode grows without bound iff its growth rate has positive real part.

results.title: A Fourier mode grows iff `J - k² D` has an eigenvalue with positive real part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Fourier mode grows iff `J - k² D` has an eigenvalue with positive real part.

results.title: Homogeneous mode is stable for stable kinetics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The homogeneous mode `k = 0` is stable when the kinetics are stable (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`).

results.title: Mode instability iff the dispersion polynomial is negative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `tr J < 0` and `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, mode `k` is unstable iff `h(k²) < 0`.

results.title: Diffusion-driven instability (Turing 1952)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`), `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, and `det (J - k² D) < 0`, then the homogeneous mode is stable while mode `k` is unstable.

results.title: Minimum value of the dispersion polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The value of the dispersion polynomial at its minimizer: `h(k_c²) = det J - (d_v f_u + d_u g_v)² / (4 d_u d_v)`.

results.title: Critical squared wavenumber minimizes the dispersion polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The critical squared wavenumber minimizes the dispersion polynomial over all real `q`.

results.title: Turing condition in squared form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Turing condition in squared form: `2 √(d_u d_v det J) < S` iff `0 < S` and `4 d_u d_v det J < S²`, where `S = d_v f_u + d_u g_v`. This holds for all real inputs: when `d_u d_v det J < 0`, `Real.sqrt` returns `0` and both sides reduce to `0 < S`.

results.title: Turing's criterion for diffusion-driven instability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `d_u, d_v > 0` and `0 < det J`, the dispersion polynomial is negative at some `q ≥ 0` iff `2 √(d_u d_v det J) < d_v f_u + d_u g_v`.

results.title: Turing's criterion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`) and `d_u, d_v > 0`, some Fourier mode is unstable iff `d_v f_u + d_u g_v > 2 √(d_u d_v det J)`.

results.title: Critical wavenumber is unstable under Turing's criterion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under Turing's criterion the critical wavenumber `k_c = √(k_c²)` is itself unstable (and `0 < k_c²`).

results.title: Critical wavenumber at the Turing bifurcation threshold
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At the bifurcation threshold `d_v f_u + d_u g_v = 2 √(d_u d_v det J)` the critical squared wavenumber is `k_c² = √(det J / (d_u d_v))` and `h(k_c²) = 0`.

results.title: `f_u` and `g_v` have opposite signs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion and `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, diffusion-driven instability forces `f_u g_v < 0`.

results.title: The inhibitor diffuses faster
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the activator-inhibitor sign pattern (`u` is the activator, `0 < f_u`; then `g_v < 0` follows from `tr J < 0`), diffusion-driven instability of a kinetically stable state forces `d_u < d_v`.

results.title: Dispersion polynomial is negative exactly on the unstable band
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `d_u, d_v > 0`, the dispersion polynomial is negative exactly on the open band `(q₋, q₊)`, which is nonempty iff the discriminant is positive.

results.title: Neumann modes have zero flux at the boundary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Neumann mode `cos(k_n x)` has zero flux at both ends of `[0, L]`: the `x`-derivative of the Fourier mode with wavenumber `k_n = n π / L` vanishes at `x = 0` and `x = L`.

results.title: Finite domain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On `[0, L]` with Neumann boundary conditions, if `tr J < 0` and `d_u, d_v > 0`, mode `n` is unstable iff `k_n² = (n π / L)²` lies in the unstable band `(q₋, q₊)` (which requires a positive discriminant).

results.title: Only finitely many Neumann modes are unstable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Only finitely many Neumann modes are unstable on `[0, L]` (for `d_u, d_v, L > 0`, any `J`).

results.title: Small domains admit no pattern
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the first nonhomogeneous mode already lies beyond the band, `q₊ ≤ (π / L)²`, then no Neumann mode is unstable on `[0, L]`.

results.title: Long intervals have a squared Neumann wavenumber in any given band
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every long enough interval has a squared Neumann wavenumber inside a given nonempty open band `(qlo, qhi)` with `0 < qhi`: there is `L₀ > 0` such that for all `L ≥ L₀` some `(n π / L)²` lies in `(qlo, qhi)`.

results.title: Large domains pattern
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under Turing's criterion, every long enough interval `[0, L]` has an unstable Neumann mode.

results.title: Schnakenberg reaction kinetics
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Schnakenberg's reaction terms `(f, g) = (a - u + u² v, b - u² v)` as a map on `x = (u, v) : Fin 2 → ℝ`, with source rates `a, b` (biologically `a, b > 0`).

results.title: Steady state of the Schnakenberg kinetics
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The homogeneous steady state `(u₀, v₀) = (a + b, b / (a + b)²)` of the Schnakenberg kinetics (meaningful for `a + b ≠ 0`; at `a + b = 0` the division gives the junk `v₀ = 0`).

results.title: Jacobian of the Schnakenberg kinetics at its steady state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Jacobian of the Schnakenberg kinetics at its steady state, `[[(b - a) / (a + b), (a + b)²], [-2 b / (a + b), -(a + b)²]]`.

results.title: Schnakenberg steady state is an equilibrium
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `(a + b, b / (a + b)²)` is a steady state of the Schnakenberg kinetics when `a + b ≠ 0`.

results.title: Computation of the Schnakenberg Jacobian at the steady state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Jacobian matrix of the Schnakenberg kinetics at the steady state is `schnakenbergJacobian a b`.

results.title: Determinant of the Schnakenberg Jacobian
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `det J = (a + b)²` for the Schnakenberg Jacobian (`a + b ≠ 0`).

results.title: Stability of the Schnakenberg steady state without diffusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Schnakenberg steady state is stable without diffusion iff `b - a < (a + b)³` (for `0 < a + b`; then `0 < det J` automatically).

results.title: Turing instability of the Schnakenberg kinetics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Turing instability of the Schnakenberg kinetics (Murray 2003, ch. 2). With `d_u = 1`, `d_v = d > 0`, `0 < a + b` and `b - a < (a + b)³` (stable without diffusion), some Fourier mode is unstable iff `2 √d (a + b)² < d (b - a) - (a + b)³`.

results.title: Gierer–Meinhardt activator-inhibitor kinetics
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Gierer–Meinhardt activator-inhibitor kinetics in Murray's nondimensional form `(f, g) = (a - b u + u² / v, u² - v)` on `x = (u, v)` (biologically `a, b > 0` and `u, v > 0`; at `v = 0` the division gives the junk `u² / 0 = 0`).

results.title: Steady state of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The homogeneous steady state `(u₀, v₀) = ((a + 1) / b, ((a + 1) / b)²)` of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics (meaningful for `b ≠ 0`, `a + 1 ≠ 0`).

results.title: Jacobian of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at its steady state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Jacobian of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at its steady state, `[[b (1 - a) / (1 + a), -(b / (a + 1))²], [2 (a + 1) / b, -1]]`.

results.title: Gierer–Meinhardt steady state is an equilibrium
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `((a + 1) / b, ((a + 1) / b)²)` is a steady state of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics when `a + 1 ≠ 0` and `b ≠ 0`.

results.title: Computation of the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian at the steady state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Jacobian matrix of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at the steady state is `giererMeinhardtJacobian a b`.

results.title: Determinant of the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `det J = b` for the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian (`a + 1 ≠ 0`, `b ≠ 0`).

results.title: Stability of the Gierer–Meinhardt steady state without diffusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Gierer–Meinhardt steady state is stable without diffusion iff `b (1 - a) < 1 + a` (for `0 < a + 1`; then `0 < det J = b` for `0 < b`).

results.title: Turing instability of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With `d_u = 1`, `d_v = d > 0`, `0 < a + 1`, `0 < b` and `b (1 - a) < 1 + a` (stable without diffusion), some Fourier mode is unstable iff `2 √(d b) < d b (1 - a) / (1 + a) - 1`.

results.title: Turn weight between two lattice directions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The turn weight from direction `μ` to direction `ν`: `1` straight, `ω` for a left turn, `0` for a U-turn, `ω⁻¹` for a right turn.

results.title: Trace of a power as a power sum of characteristic roots
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The trace of `φ ^ k` is the sum of the `k`-th powers of the roots of the characteristic polynomial of `φ`. See also `Matrix.trace_eq_sum_roots_charpoly`, the case `k = 1`.

results.title: Walk-series square root of det(1 − Λ)
